authority: R-167 v2.1 is additive to v2.0 and preserves every earlier theorem, boundary, and historical checkpoint. It adds two narrowly scoped children. First, a translate/orientation/history-uniform twentieth endpoint-coordinate moment implies the fixed-edge growing corridor with the sharp polynomial bound 2916 c^2 M20 R^6 L^-16; p=5 and L=R^(2/5) give R^-2/5 while the bounded-cutoff factorial has logarithm -R log(R)/5+O(R). A separate conditional theorem reduces that twentieth moment to a source/translate-uniform local fifth Gibbs moment, a one-site quartic elliptic embedding, and simultaneous-bond fifth graph propagation. Second, the full two-site oscillator edge has, under explicit low/high data and a strict Schur margin, exactly one even and one odd low eigenvalue and an explicit third-to-second gap; nested parity-preserving onsite spectral Ritz restrictions retain the same bounds and converge to the full edge form. Neither child proves the missing Q3 fifth-moment inputs, n-to-infinity/all-exhaustion common alpha, quasi-local many-edge rank-two QPS transfer, or an oscillator-lattice GNS gap.

pure_bond_tail_theorem.setup: V_cross=-c sum_<xy> q_x dot q_y, B_delta=exp(-i delta V_cross/hbar). Every bounded coordinate multiplier F(q_S) commutes with B_delta; affiliated weighted coordinate multipliers strongly commute on their natural finite-moment forms.
pure_bond_tail_theorem.invariance: B_delta^* F(q_S) B_delta=F(q_S) in both orientations. Coordinate tail projections, finite-moment weighted coordinate tails, and coordinate cutoff-tail squares are unchanged by a pure all-bond layer.
pure_bond_tail_theorem.cutoff_identity: For coordinate cutoff V_cross,L, W_L=V_cross-V_cross,L and B_delta,L=exp(-i delta V_cross,L/hbar), every finite-volume type-I normal state sigma with sigma(W_L^2)<infinity obeys both Hilbert-Schmidt identities ||(B_delta-B_delta,L)sigma^(1/2)||_2^2=||sigma^(1/2)(B_delta-B_delta,L)||_2^2=sigma(4 sin^2(delta W_L/(2hbar)))<=delta^2 sigma(W_L^2)/hbar^2.
pure_bond_tail_theorem.consequence: An exact state-weighted all-bond telescope pays no exp(C L^2) operator-norm multiplier. The missing input is the W_L^2 tail in intermediate onsite-interspersed history states, in both orientations.
pure_bond_tail_theorem.scope: This is an exact single-layer and telescope identity. It does not bound onsite history tails or prove convergence of the complete split product.

local_measured_renyi_reduction.setup: For fixed finite S and alpha>1 put theta=(alpha-1)/alpha. Let nu_0,S be the reference distribution of X_S=max_(x in S)|q_x|, and nu_P,S^plus/minus the distributions after a partial history and its adjoint.
local_measured_renyi_reduction.minimal_target: Uniformly in volume, source, mesh, partial history and orientation, require nu_P,S^plus/minus(X_S>u)<=C_(alpha,T,S) nu_0,S(X_S>u)^theta for u>=L_0.
local_measured_renyi_reduction.measured_renyi_sufficient: A stronger checkable condition is the classical coordinate-algebra bound integral (d nu_P,S^plus/minus/d nu_0,S)^alpha d nu_0,S<=Q_(alpha,T,S). It is strictly weaker than global quantum sandwiched Renyi.
local_measured_renyi_reduction.tail: If nu_0,S(X_S>u)<=M_a|S|exp(-a u^2), Holder gives the two-orientation probability bound 2 Q^(1/alpha)(M_a|S|)^theta exp(-theta a L^2). Layer cake gives 2 Q^(1/alpha)(M_a|S|)^theta exp(-bL^2)(L^4+2L^2/b+2/b^2), b=theta a.
local_measured_renyi_reduction.scope: This closes only the fixed-finite-S implication from a local measured likelihood bound to a weighted coordinate tail. A growing corridor additionally requires a bound uniform over translates of the relevant fixed bond shapes, or an explicit growth envelope for Q_{alpha,T,S_R} that is absorbable as R and L grow. No such onsite-interspersed Q3LOCK bound or uniform-growth estimate is proved.

q3_semiclassical_onsite.normalization: For R=-r>0, mu=lambda/g>0, v=sqrt(R/g), E_star=R^2/g and h_sc=hbar g/(sqrt(chi) R^(3/2)), the shifted one-site operator is exactly E_star[-h_sc^2 Delta/2+W_mu], with W_mu=1/4 sum_e(x_e^2-1)^2+mu/4 sum_{Q3 edges}(x_e-x_f)^2(x_e^2+x_f^2).

q3_semiclassical_onsite.imported_theorem: For every fixed mu>0 there is h_0(mu)>0 such that 0<h_sc<h_0 gives a simple even/odd Aut(Q3)-singlet doublet. For every eta>0, delta_1=epsilon_1-epsilon_0<=E_star C_eta exp(-(S_0-eta)/h_sc); Gamma=epsilon_2-epsilon_0=E_star[sqrt(2)h_sc+O(h_sc^(3/2))]; m=<phi_0,q_e phi_1>=v[1+O(h_sc)]; a_j=<phi_j,q_e^2 phi_j>=v^2[1+O(h_sc)]; b_j=<phi_j,q_e^4 phi_j>=v^4[1+O(h_sc)]; and the safe localization consequence is a_1-a_0=O(v^2 h_sc). No exponential weighted-even-observable splitting rate is imported without a separate Agmon-overlap theorem.
q3_semiclassical_onsite.scope: This is an existential small-h_sc theorem for fixed mu>0. It does not certify a numerical h_0 for the repository's r=-9 fixture and is not a many-body phase or GNS-gap theorem.

On a z=6 periodic cubic lattice this is delta_eff=delta_1+4zc d_2=delta_1+24c d_2. Open finite boxes have the exact site-dependent boundary field shown above.
exact_low_band_compression.residual_data: With a^2=max_j(a_j-m^2)=||Qq_eP||^2 and b^2=max_j(b_j-a_j^2)=||Qq_e^2P||^2, one bond obeys ||(1-P_xP_y)B_xyP_xP_y||<=8c[b+2ma+a^2]. For k=h_site-epsilon_0-delta_1P_1>=Gamma Q, R_e=q_e-ms and every t>0, ||R_e psi||^2<=(1+t)a^2||Ppsi||^2+(1+t^(-1))A_Q<Qpsi,kQpsi>, A_Q=v^2/Gamma+2sqrt(epsilon_0+Gamma)/(Gamma sqrt(g)).
exact_low_band_compression.corridor: For g=lambda=chi=hbar=1, r=-N^4, c=N^-4, h_sc=N^-6, J tends to 8, Gamma is asymptotic to sqrt(2)N^2, a=O(N^-1), b=O(N), the one-bond low/high block is O(N^-3), cA_Q=O(N^-2), the mixed-form coefficient c m sqrt(A_Q)=O(N^-1), delta_eff=O(N^-6)+O(N^8 exp(-(S_0-eta)N^6)), and the registered infrared quantity satisfies A_0 asymptotic to (2/9)N^4. Thus the model-side low/high ratios and effective field can vanish without collapsing the Ising scale or violating the IR lower condition.

unbounded_block_qps_boundary.mismatch: The published Del Vecchio-Frohlich-Pizzo theorem assumes a rank-one onsite vacuum and concludes a unique ground state with a uniform gap. Its local projectors are tensor products of rank-one vacuum projections. The introductory degenerate-extension remark is not a stated theorem for a rank-two onsite band whose global low space has dimension 2^|Lambda|.
unbounded_block_qps_boundary.why_rank_one_fails: Choosing phi_0 alone makes the onsite gap delta_1 exponentially small, while the desired Ising scale J stays order one in the semiclassical corridor, so the published small-coupling theorem cannot be applied phase-blindly.
unbounded_block_qps_boundary.surviving_route: Prove a new volume-uniform rank-two band Lie-Schwinger/Feshbach theorem that subtracts the exact H_low block and yields a bounded effective spin interaction small enough for finite-dimensional two-phase QPS, or prove an equivalent spectral-cutoff removal theorem preserving both phases and a common positive gap.
unbounded_block_qps_boundary.scope: This is a direct-import mismatch, not a no-go for a future rank-two unbounded block theorem and not a counterexample to the exact Q3LOCK broken-sector gap.

full_hamiltonian_gibbs_resummation.hypotheses: In one finite volume let H and H_L=H-W_L be self-adjoint and bounded below, let rho=Z^-1 exp(-beta H), and assume the two Duhamel formulas hold on a common invariant form core with W_L rho^(1/2) and rho^(1/2) W_L Hilbert-Schmidt; equivalently rho(W_L^2)<infinity for self-adjoint W_L.
full_hamiltonian_gibbs_resummation.two_orientation_bound: For U(t)=exp(-itH/hbar) and U_L(t)=exp(-itH_L/hbar), both ||(U-U_L)rho^(1/2)||_2 and ||rho^(1/2)(U-U_L)||_2 are at most |t| rho(W_L^2)^(1/2)/hbar. One opposite Duhamel ordering is used per orientation; rho commutes only with the full U.
full_hamiltonian_gibbs_resummation.state_stability: Because U rho U*=rho, ||rho-U_L rho U_L*||_1 is at most 2|t|rho(W_L^2)^(1/2)/hbar.
full_hamiltonian_gibbs_resummation.bounded_context_transfer: If A rho^(1/2)=rho^(1/2) C_A and A* rho^(1/2)=rho^(1/2) C_Astar with both half-modular contexts bounded, the two state-weighted automorphism seminorms transfer with factors ||A||+||C_A|| and ||A||+||C_Astar||. A sufficient narrow class is a finite Bohr-frequency decomposition A=sum A_omega, [H,A_omega]=omega A_omega, |omega|<=Omega, sum||A_omega||<infinity; then each half-modular context is bounded by exp(beta Omega/2) sum||A_omega||. Mere matrix bandwidth without this projective decomposition is not asserted.
full_hamiltonian_gibbs_resummation.scope: This is a finite-volume static-full-Gibbs unitary and state theorem. It does not pass arbitrary bounded contexts, control onsite-interspersed history states, prove a local automorphism limit, or close the common-alpha parent.
full_hamiltonian_gibbs_resummation.q3_form_domain_instantiation: For the registered finite-volume Q3 hard/form-cutoff pair, H and H_L are the closed form sums on the common quartic form domain; W_L is a real quadratic coordinate multiplier (possibly hard-tail restricted), W_L^2 has quartic growth, and the existing finite-volume Gibbs coordinate moments give rho(W_L^2)<infinity. Truncate W_L spectrally/formwise to bounded W_L,M, apply bounded Duhamel, then use form/strong-resolvent convergence and W_L,M rho^(1/2)->W_L rho^(1/2) in S2 to close the displayed bounds. This instantiation is for that hard/form pair; a differently defined smooth clipped-coordinate cutoff requires its own common-domain/form-convergence check.

arbitrary_context_no_go.fixture: For rho_p=diag(1-p,p), H=(pi hbar/t0)|1><1|, beta=t0 log((1-p)/p)/(pi hbar), H_L=0, and A=sigma_x, both squared weighted unitary errors are 4p and rho_p(W^2)=(pi hbar/t0)^2 p, while both one-sided weighted automorphism-error norms are exactly 2 and their sum-# squared is 8. Both evolved density matrices equal rho_p, so their trace distance is exactly zero.
arbitrary_context_no_go.consequence: As p tends to zero, static Gibbs weighted-unitary convergence and even exact state stability do not imply arbitrary-context automorphism convergence. The missing half-modular context norm grows as sqrt((1-p)/p).
arbitrary_context_no_go.scope: This rejects only the automatic arbitrary-context L2 upgrade. It is not a no-go for a bounded half-modular core, a fixed Bohr-band projective class, or Q3LOCK dynamics.

fixed_edge_restricted_tail_corridor.edge_reduction: For W_R,L=sum_(e in E_R) w_e,L and m_R=|E_R|, pointwise/form Cauchy gives W_R,L^2<=m_R sum_e w_e,L^2. If w_e,L^2<=c^2 X_e^4 1_(X_e>L) and the v1.9 two-orientation fixed-edge bound is uniform over all required translates and orientations, the two-orientation W-square sum is at most m_R^2 c^2 K_edge(L).

With alpha=2, theta=1/2, a=2, b=1, Q=4, M_a=1/2 and |S_e|=2, K_edge(L)=4 exp(-L^2)(L^4+2L^2+2). Taking L_R=sqrt(R) gives the explicit upper 1296 R^6 exp(-R)(R^2+2R+2), which tends to zero; e^R>=R^10/10! gives an elementary rational majorant.
fixed_edge_restricted_tail_corridor.covariance_boundary: On a periodic cubic torus, translation covariance alone reduces the supremum to three canonical bond orientations, not one; cubic rotations are additionally needed to identify them. Open boundaries, nonuniform sources, local insertions, or ordered partial histories can break this reduction and require an explicit uniform supremum.
fixed_edge_restricted_tail_corridor.scope: This closes the deterministic reduction from a uniform fixed-bond restricted-tail input to one growing corridor. It does not prove that input for Q3LOCK histories.

They are not constants for the separately defined smooth clipped-coordinate Q_L Hamiltonians; transferring them to a smooth clip requires a new pointwise domination and form-convergence audit.

homogeneous_tilted_edge_no_go.fixture: Tilt the standard two-coordinate Gaussian by f_kappa(x,y)=sqrt(1-kappa^2) exp(kappa xy) with kappa=3/4. The precision is positive with determinant 7/16, so all moments are finite and endpoint swap/global-sign symmetries hold. Each marginal variance is 16/7, so its tail exponent 7/32 is slower than the alpha=2 reference-power exponent 1/4. The required fixed-edge Holder tail ratio is unbounded; the order-two likelihood integral diverges because the squared-tilt precision determinant is -5/4.
homogeneous_tilted_edge_no_go.scope: This is only a two-site-periodic or homogeneous-dimer implication no-go from static Gaussianity, endpoint symmetry and finite moments. It is not a fully one-site-translation-invariant lattice fixture and not a Q3 history, locality, or dynamics nonexistence theorem.

global_feshbach_relative_form_precursor.setup: Let P_Lambda=P^(tensor Lambda), Q_Lambda=1-P_Lambda, and K_Lambda=sum_x k_x>=Gamma sum_x Q_x, retaining the nonnegative exact Q3 bonds. Before subtracting any extensive scalar used to rewrite the low TFIM, the absolute finite-volume compression obeys Q_Lambda H Q_Lambda>=Gamma Q_Lambda and for E<Gamma has the exact Feshbach operator F(E)=PHP-E-PHQ(QHQ-E)^(-1)QHP. This is absolute-energy algebra, not thermodynamic isolation of a volume-dependent ground band.
global_feshbach_relative_form_precursor.overlap_and_self_energy: In an arbitrary finite cubic subgraph, a nearest-neighbour bond overlaps, including itself, with at most 1+2(z-1)=11 bonds for z<=6; equality holds for bulk edges and sufficiently large periodic tori, while boundary edges can have fewer. If every local low/high block is bounded by epsilon, ||QHP||^2<=11|E_Lambda|epsilon^2 and the positive self-energy is at most 11|E_Lambda|epsilon^2/(Gamma-E). This is extensive.
global_feshbach_relative_form_precursor.relative_form_coefficients: For one bond define P_xy=P_xP_y and Q_xy=1-P_xy. With Young parameters u,t>0, the v1.9 centered estimate gives eta_b=8c(1+u^-1)(1+t^-1)A_Q and nu_b=16c[(1+u)m^2+(1+u^-1)(1+t)a^2]. Its diagonal local-high compression satisfies Q_xy B_xy Q_xy <=(eta_b+nu_b/Gamma) Q_xy(k_x+k_y)Q_xy because Q_xy(k_x+k_y)Q_xy>=Gamma Q_xy. This is not the distinct full centered-residual/off-diagonal estimate epsilon=8c(b+2ma+a^2). Summing diagonal high forms gives zeta=z(eta_b+nu_b/Gamma). At u=t=1, eta_b=32cA_Q and nu_b=32cm^2+64ca^2; in the N corridor epsilon=O(N^-3), zeta=O(N^-2).
global_feshbach_relative_form_precursor.scope: This is a finite-volume absolute-energy below-one-high-mode Feshbach identity, an at-most-11 overlap bound, and a diagonal local-high relative-form precursor. It is not thermodynamic ground-band isolation, a quasi-local block diagonalization, cutoff removal, or a QPS-norm bound for the oscillator effective interaction.

compressed_tfim_two_phase_qps.reference: For delta_eff=0, assign each positive-coordinate cubic bond once. The four-spin forward-star block J sum_(i=1)^3(1-s_0 s_i) has exact spectrum 0 (multiplicity 2), 2J (6), 4J (6), 6J (2), hence two product ground vectors and local gap 2J. Use the auxiliary selector u sum_x(1-s_x); with the convention k_u=d(e_plus-e_minus)/du, the split is k=(0,-2). The transverse perturbation delta_eff sum_x P_1,x is finite range and Z2 invariant, so symmetry pins the local coexistence surface to u=0.
compressed_tfim_two_phase_qps.imported_conclusion: Yarotskii's stated two-phase quantum Pirogov-Sinai theorem gives, for an existential epsilon_Y>0 and |delta_eff|/(2J)<epsilon_Y, the two pure translation-invariant infinite-lattice phases of the exact compressed finite-spin TFIM, exponential clustering, and a positive GNS Hamiltonian gap in each selected phase.
compressed_tfim_two_phase_qps.scope: This is only the exact compressed TFIM. It asserts no finite-torus exact degeneracy, explicit epsilon_Y or N_0, repository r=-9 applicability, rank-two oscillator transfer, or oscillator GNS gap.

extensive_self_energy_no_go.fixture: A one-high-level block coupled with equal amplitude epsilon to M low basis vectors has self-energy epsilon^2/(Gamma-E) times the M-by-M all-ones matrix. Its norm is M epsilon^2/(Gamma-E) but every off-diagonal entry is nonzero.
extensive_self_energy_no_go.consequence: An extensive global Feshbach norm estimate alone carries no interaction-decay or polymer-locality data and cannot be promoted automatically to a two-phase QPS norm.
extensive_self_energy_no_go.scope: This rejects only the automatic inference from a global extensive bound. It is not a no-go for a linked-cluster, Lie-Schwinger, or local resolvent expansion.

twentieth_moment_fixed_edge_corridor.definition: For a tested edge e and every required finite volume, compact source, split mesh, partial history, translate and orientation, put X_e=max(|q_x|,|q_y|) and M20=sup[sigma_plus(X_e^20)+sigma_minus(X_e^20)].
twentieth_moment_fixed_edge_corridor.theorem: If M20<infinity and w_e,L^2<=c^2 X_e^4 1_(X_e>L), then the two-orientation corridor satisfies sigma_plus(W_R,L^2)+sigma_minus(W_R,L^2)<=m_R^2 c^2 M20 L^-16<=2916 c^2 M20 R^6 L^-16, because m_R=6R(2R+1)^2<=54R^3 and X^4 1_(X>L)<=X^20 L^-16.
twentieth_moment_fixed_edge_corridor.scale: For a uniform 4p-th moment and L=R^gamma the exponent is 6-4gamma(p-1). The bounded-cutoff factorial requires gamma<1/2, so the minimal possible integer is p=5. The explicit choice gamma=2/5 gives R^-2/5 and log[(C R^(4/5))^R/R!]=-R log(R)/5+O(R).

conditional_fifth_graph_transport.definitions: k_(x,h) is the positive shifted exact onsite Hamiltonian. Let m5=sup phi_(Lambda,h)(k_(x,h)^5), d5=sup || |q|^10 k_h^(-5/2)||, mu_z=exp(-mu d(z,e)) with both endpoint weights one, K_e=sum_z mu_z k_(z,h), and S_mu=sum_z mu_z. Distinct-site k_z strongly commute.
conditional_fifth_graph_transport.C1_form_hypothesis: For the simultaneous all-cross-bond generator V_x and B_delta=exp(-i delta V_x/hbar), K_e^5 has an invariant form domain, the quadratic-form derivative is <B_delta psi,(i/hbar)[V_x,K_e^5]B_delta psi>, and G5=sup ||K_e^(-5/2)(i/hbar)[V_x,K_e^5]K_e^(-5/2)|| is finite uniformly in all declared indices.
conditional_fifth_graph_transport.commutator_expansion: With J_e=(i/hbar)[V_x,K_e], G5 is bounded by ||K_e^(-1/2)J_eK_e^(-1/2)||+2||K_e^(1/2)J_eK_e^(-3/2)||+2||K_e^(3/2)J_eK_e^(-5/2)||. The exact grouped coefficients are 1,2,2.
conditional_fifth_graph_transport.transport: The graph norm obeys ||K_e^(5/2)B_delta K_e^(-5/2)||<=exp(G5|delta|/2). Onsite product steps commute with K_e; bond steps of total absolute time at most T therefore give each orientation a K_e^5 moment at most exp(G5 T) S_mu^5 m5.
conditional_fifth_graph_transport.sharp_result: Strong commutativity gives phi(K_e^5)<=S_mu^5 m5, while X_e^20<=|q_x|^20+|q_y|^20<=d5^2(k_x^5+k_y^5)<=d5^2K_e^5. Hence M20<=2 d5^2 exp(G5 T) S_mu^5 m5.
conditional_fifth_graph_transport.scope: The theorem is conditional. Existing static sharp-coordinate exponential moments do not establish m5, and the existing low graph endpoint does not supply the s=5/2 transport or the two extra commutator rungs.

all_order_graph_growth_no_go.fixture: For K=diag(1,4), V=sigma_x and hbar=1, C_m=K^(-m/2)i[V,K^m]K^(-m/2) has exact norm 2^m-2^(-m). For A_m(t)=K^(m/2)exp(-itV)K^(-m/2), A_m(t)^*A_m(t)=I+tC_m+O(t^2), and the right Dini derivative of log||A_m(t)||, equivalently t down to zero after maximizing over plus/minus t, is ||C_m||/2.
all_order_graph_growth_no_go.consequence: Any bound ||A_m(t)||<=exp(G_m|t|/2) forces G_m>=2^m-2^(-m). Therefore low-order graph information does not automatically give a quadratic-in-m all-order hierarchy.
all_order_graph_growth_no_go.scope: This abstract normalized-commutator fixture rejects only an automatic all-m inference. A Q3 embedding would additionally require a proved nonzero onsite spectral transition. It does not reject existence of the fixed m=5 constant G5.

static_moment_low_graph_no_go.fixture: Let K_N=diag(1,N^4), q_N=diag(0,N), H_N=diag(0,N^4), rho_N proportional to exp(-H_N), V_N=sigma_y/N^4 and U_N(delta)=exp(-i delta V_N), with delta nonzero and N^4>=|delta|. Then d5=1 and rho_N(K_N^5)<=1+(5/e)^5. For every 0<=s<=1, ||K_N^s U_N(delta)K_N^(-s)||<=1+|delta|, yet the exact fifth normalized commutator constant is G5=N^6-N^(-14).
static_moment_low_graph_no_go.history_tail: Using sin(x)^2>=x^2/4 for |x|<=1 and the ground Gibbs weight at least one half, each of the plus/minus history orientations has q_N^20 moment at least delta^2 N^12/8, so their sum is at least delta^2 N^12/4.
static_moment_low_graph_no_go.scope: This rejects automatic promotion from static moments plus graph control only through 0<=s<=1 to a uniform twentieth history moment. It is not a Q3 dynamics no-go and is consistent with the conditional theorem once the growing G5 is retained.

full_oscillator_edge_cluster.setup: For z=6 set h_xy=[(h_x-epsilon0)+(h_y-epsilon0)]/z+B_xy with B_xy=(c/2)sum_e(q_xe-q_ye)^2. Let P be the onsite even/odd doublet, P0 the aligned s-spin span, L the low misaligned span and Q=1-P_xP_y. Put Cb=8c(a0-m^2), fb=delta1/z+4cd2, eb=Cb+fb, J=8cm^2, epsilon=8c(b+2ma+a^2), A=eb+2J and D=Gamma/z.
full_oscillator_edge_cluster.compressions: The exact diagonal compressions are P0 h_xy P0=eb P0 and L h_xy L=(eb+2J)L; Q h_xy Q>=D Q and ||Q h_xy P_xP_y||<=epsilon. Generally P0 h_xy L is nonzero and has norm |fb|, so no block-diagonal or invariant-subspace statement is made.
full_oscillator_edge_cluster.sharp_minmax: If h_xy commutes with global parity, is nonnegative with compact resolvent, eb>=0, J>0, D>eb and epsilon^2<2J(D-eb), define gb=(A+D-sqrt((D-A)^2+4epsilon^2))/2. Then gb>eb; there is exactly one even and one odd eigenvalue at most eb, lambda3>=gb, and lambda3-lambda2>=gb-eb. When D>A, gb-eb>=2J-epsilon^2/(D-A).
full_oscillator_edge_cluster.relative_form: With k=h_site-epsilon0-delta1P1, h0=(k_x+k_y)/z+J(1-s_xs_y), gamma0=min(Gamma/z,2J), rho_b=eta_b+nu_b/Gamma and ell_b=8c(a0-m^2)+8c|d2|, for tau>0 the remainder obeys |<V>|<=alpha<h0>+beta||.||^2 with alpha=z[rho_b+J/Gamma+epsilon^2/(tau Gamma)] and beta=2delta1/z+ell_b+tau. If alpha<1 and Delta_rf=(1-alpha)gamma0-2beta>0, the same parity count holds and lambda3-lambda2>=Delta_rf.
full_oscillator_edge_cluster.spectral_cutoff_removal: For nested parity-preserving onsite spectral projections Pi_M>=P whose union is a quartic form core, restrict the original full form by Pi_M tensor Pi_M. The same constants hold and the Ritz eigenvalues decrease to the full edge eigenvalues, preserving the uniform lower gap. Replacing q by Pi_M q Pi_M before squaring is not this construction because Pi_M q^2 Pi_M need not equal (Pi_M q Pi_M)^2.
full_oscillator_edge_cluster.asymptotic_scope: In the v1.9 N corridor, eb=O(N^-6), epsilon=O(N^-3), D is asymptotic to a positive constant times N^2 and 2J tends to 16, so the sharp local edge gap tends to 16 with O(N^-8) mixing correction. The relative-form alpha=O(N^-2) and beta=O(N^-3). This is local edge coercivity only, not a linked-cluster elimination, oscillator QPS theorem, or oscillator-lattice GNS gap.
